Understand your M3 project

This is a study guide to the actual code in this checkout, inspected on 15 October 2026. It includes the project structure, how data moves, each file's job, and source lines paired with explanations. Start here, then use the four source chapters in the order below. The browser edition has navigation and search.

The current implementation is M3 only, using the official 5G-NIDD release. The earlier conversation proposed a shared M1/M2/M3 interface, but the present app is an M3 results dashboard. The current code and its evidence boundaries take precedence over that older plan.

Read in this order

1. Read this overview and the concrete observation example below.

2. In backend.md, begin with config.py, data.py, model.py, and engine.py. These explain what a model receives, learns, and predicts.

3. Read metrics.py, store.py, provenance.py, and analysis.py in the same chapter. These explain where numbers come from and how evidence is saved.

4. Read packets.py, ground_truth.py, labels.py, sflow.py, and live.py. These explain how real network packets become model observations.

5. Read sdn-and-data-tools.md for the downloader, label preparation, controller, topology and diagnostics.

6. Read frontend.md for React, API requests, plots, filtering and frontend tests. Read backend api.py and cli.py alongside it.

7. Read tests-and-configuration.md to understand exactly what the tests assert and what the two supplied configurations mean.

8. Use reference-data.md for line explanations of the dataset manifest and generated npm dependency lock. These record data/dependency identity rather than model decisions.

Every table pairs a physical line number with its original source and explanation. A statement may span several lines: the opening line explains the operation; following lines explain arguments, values, conditions and delimiters. Comments and blank lines are identified too. A frozen dataclass is not recursively immutable, and type hints alone are not runtime validation.

Local housekeeping directories also exist: .venv and .venv-sdn are installed Python environments; .tools holds local executables; .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache and __pycache__ are caches; tmp is scratch space; Partner Work contains local partner material; .git stores version history. Those are not source modules to memorize. Generated node_modules/dist, downloaded datasets and raw captures can contain many files. Their schema and role are documented without attempting to explain installed third-party library internals or millions of dataset records.

inventory.json records the exact tracked-file snapshot, each file's role, SHA256 and coverage chapter. coverage-report.json verifies that every maintained executable/configuration line and the two reference JSON files have matching numbered explanations. New guide and graph files are documentation/tool outputs created by this task.

Three workflows, with different evidence

CSV replay:
CLI -> RunConfig -> provenance -> iter_csv -> allowed flow features
    -> seeded selection with probability 1/N -> Evaluation -> OnlineDetector

Offline packet replay:
CLI -> RunConfig -> provenance -> original PCAP packets
    -> ALL original packets -> FlowLabels/WindowTruth -> window answer
    -> SELECTED packets -> WindowAccumulator -> packet-window features
    -> Evaluation -> OnlineDetector

Live collection:
Mininet hosts -> OVS (sampling happens here) -> sFlow UDP exports
    -> run_live -> decode_datagram -> WindowAccumulator
    + independently supplied timeline labels -> Evaluation -> OnlineDetector

All three:
Evaluation -> raw predictions + quality + ADWIN event records
ResourceMonitor -> process metrics + optional LabMeasurements
RunWriter -> output/runs/<run-id>/ CSVs + run_summary.json

Display:
React App -> frontend/api.ts -> FastAPI -> RunRepository -> saved evidence

Analysis:
CLI analyse -> RunRepository -> compatible groups -> repeated-trial statistics
            -> quality/cost charts + measured-bandwidth Pareto front

The CLI, model experiment, SDN controller, telemetry collector and HTTP server are separate roles. Opening the dashboard does not start learning. The controller forwards network traffic; HAT predicts alarms; there is no automatic attack-blocking/mitigation in the M3 application.

Follow one observation yourself

Consider a CSV record whose true family is UDPFlood. iter_csv keeps its allowed numeric features and Proto, and maps its target to 1. Labels, IP addresses, tools, Offset and Seq do not enter features. Suppose the seeded sampler selects it and it occurs after warm-up.

1. Evaluation.observe reads the true label as evaluation metadata and tracks the first attack, if needed.

2. OnlineDetector.predict(features) asks HAT for the attack probability. Suppose it returns 0.7. With threshold 0.5, predicted becomes 1. This example value illustrates the code; it is not an experimental result.

3. RunWriter.append writes the prediction, score, true label, latency and phase to predictions.csv.

4. QualityMetrics.update increments (1, 1), a true positive, and stores score/latency.

5. OnlineDetector.learn gives the external ADWIN error 0 because the answer was correct. It then calls HAT's learn_one(features, 1).

6. If external ADWIN signals a change, the evaluator appends a drift event. That signal does not itself reset HAT; HAT's internal adaptation is a separate mechanism.

7. Periodic summary saves and the resource thread produce readable evidence for the dashboard.

For warm-up, steps involving scored metrics and the external error monitor are skipped, but predictions are logged and HAT still learns. For an unknown label (None), the prediction is logged and neither quality scoring nor supervised learning occurs. For held-out SYNFlood during unseen-scenario warm-up, the record is excluded before prediction.

When running live, the model does not know whether traffic is malicious by magic. The code learns only when separate ground-truth annotations supply a label. Immediate labels after prediction are an experiment assumption. A real deployment needs a trustworthy label-feedback policy.

Why each measurement exists

ConceptWhat it answersCode location
PrecisionOf alarms raised, how many were correct?metrics.py
RecallOf actual attack observations, how many were caught?metrics.py
F1How well are precision and recall balanced?metrics.py
ROC-AUCDo attack observations rank above benign ones by probability?metrics.py
False-positive rateHow often does benign traffic trigger an alarm?metrics.py
Inference latencyHow long did the prediction call take?model.py, metrics.py
Detection delayTime from first known attack to first correct alarm windowengine.py
Packets-to-detectOriginal packets from attack onset through alarm window, when counts knownengine.py, ground_truth.py
Detector CPU/RSSCost of the collector/detector processresources.py
Controller CPUSeparate controller process cost, when a PID is availableresources.py
sFlow payload bandwidthExport bytes received by the collector per secondlive.py, resources.py
OpenFlow bandwidthIndependently captured controller-channel frame bytes per secondlab.py
Flow-table entriesSnapshot mean of actual OVS flow entrieslab.py
Post-drift recoveryTime to regain an agreed performance level after annotated shiftCurrently unavailable in engine.py

The same number has different meaning under different modes: CSV quality is conditional on selected flow rows; packet replay quality applies to fully labeled windows formed from unsampled original truth. An estimated offline payload proxy is not measured live network bandwidth. The software records that distinction explicitly.

Python and frontend syntax you will meet

SyntaxMeaning in this code
class X:Defines a type that groups state and methods. A new instance is made by X(...).
selfThe current object instance, supplied by Python when you call its method.
def / returnDefine a function / send its result back to the caller. Defining is not executing the body.
@dataclass(frozen=True)Generates field initialization/helpers and prevents normal field reassignment.
str \| NoneType hint allowing a string or absence; it does not validate runtime input by itself.
dict, list, tuple, setNamed-key mapping, ordered mutable sequence, fixed sequence, unique-value collection.
yield / yield fromProduce items lazily; code runs as the caller iterates, rather than building all records at once.
[x for x in values if condition]Build a collection by looping and filtering.
**dictionaryExpand named arguments or merge dictionary entries in the surrounding expression.
withEnter a context that manages release/closing, including on errors.
try / except / finallyAttempt work, handle specified exceptions, always perform final cleanup.
lambdaSmall unnamed function, commonly a sort key or safe division helper.
Path(__file__)Filesystem path to this source module, unlike paths relative to the working directory.
async / await in frontendStart an asynchronous operation and wait without blocking the browser's whole event loop.
TypeScript interface / typeDescribe data shapes to the compiler; runtime API validation is still needed.
React useStateStore UI state whose updates schedule a render.
React useEffectRun side effects such as fetching/polling, with cleanup.
React useMemo / useCallbackReuse derived values/function identities while their dependencies are unchanged.
JSX {expression}Insert a JavaScript expression into the rendered element tree.
AbortControllerCancel outstanding fetches when a selection changes or a component is cleaned up.

What is implemented and what still needs evidence

The code implements the pipeline, conservative label matching, provenance checks, raw persistence, resource collection, API, M3 frontend and analysis. That does not mean the complete scientific study has been performed. The dated docs/verification-status.md distinguishes earlier checks from pending official capture coverage, scored live attack replay, full rates/trials/scenarios, recovery analysis and final reporting. This guide did not rerun those experiments.

The optional static-build path in api.py uses parents[2]: for Project/src/m3/api.py, parents[0] is m3, parents[1] is src and parents[2] is Project. It correctly points to root frontend/dist and mounts only if that build exists. The overview API's maximum-F1 selection does not establish comparability across sources/scenarios; inspect the evidence grouping before making that claim. Application behavior was not changed by this documentation request.

Learn by predicting behavior

Before executing a command, write what files it reads, what objects it creates and what files it writes. Then compare that prediction with its implementation.

- In model.py, explain why predict has no label parameter but learn does.

- In data.py, count the 29 features and identify which source columns are intentionally excluded.

- In engine.py, point to the exact line where scoring precedes learning. Explain how an unknown label changes the path.

- Explain why selecting scenario="drift" is insufficient to create a drift experiment.

- Draw the two parallel paths for original packet truth versus sampled packet features.

- In store.py, explain why readers see either the old or new JSON summary rather than a half-written file.

- In analysis.py, explain why an efficient Pareto point is not automatically the selected knee.

- In App.tsx, trace one selected run from state change to request, validation and rendered metric.

- Read a test assertion, intentionally predict its expected result on paper, then explain the implementation that makes it pass.

The goal is to be able to explain an input's path, defend the experiment assumptions, and identify what would change if you edited a line. You do not need to memorize library source or generated dependency hashes.

src/m3/config.py

Experiment configuration and validation. RunConfig is an immutable description of one run. Defaults supply omitted JSON values. Construction validates values immediately, before collectors or replay readers start. A scenario name records intent; it does not construct a drift scenario or rearrange a trace.

Snapshot: 93 lines; SHA256 330794a520a634829a4a0f1e9c19564f59c513e052324a59c6a974a1e1fa92dc.

Named operations

- RunConfig (L11): Frozen dataclass: fields are configuration values with defaults; type hints describe intended types, while __post_init__ performs the actual checks.

- RunConfig.__post_init__ (L36): Runs automatically after dataclass initialization; invalid configuration raises ValueError before an experiment starts.

- RunConfig.to_dict (L84): Serializes the dataclass for saved configuration/provenance; this returns a dictionary, not a JSON string.

- RunConfig.load (L88): Reads UTF-8 JSON, rejects unknown keys, then constructs RunConfig and triggers all validation.

src/m3/data.py

CSV records, feature extraction, and audit. Converts official CSV rows into Record objects. The allowlist is the boundary between model features and evaluation-only labels. A CSV row index is stored as time for bookkeeping only; it does not establish physical time or natural chronology.

Snapshot: 119 lines; SHA256 9e8ac45f7820a09082877768e7e0b85cbeaf13a1b7d8a5ff0c4d1a9421458e9f.

Named operations

- Record (L29): Immutable transport object shared by data readers, windowing, and Evaluation; label and family are metadata, not features.

- binary_label (L37): Returns 1 for the three in-scope floods, 0 for compatible benign labels, and None for excluded families; contradictions raise errors.

- extract_flow_features (L52): Uses only the feature allowlist; each numeric feature gets a missing-value flag, non-finite values become zero, and Proto becomes lowercase.

- iter_csv (L69): Lazily yields one Record at a time from a CSV; validates essential columns and malformed rows before handing records to the engine.

- audit_csv (L90): Counts rows, attack families, missing fields and exact duplicate row signatures without training. The duplicate-signature set grows with dataset size.

The 14 numeric CSV columns describe duration, packet/byte totals, direction-specific totals/means/TTL/rates. Their exact publisher semantics and units must be checked against the data dictionary. The extractor produces 14 values plus 14 missing flags and Proto: 29 features. Missing flags prevent a substituted zero from pretending the source really measured zero.

src/m3/model.py

The actual online learner. Wraps the installed River Hoeffding Adaptive Tree. It is one incremental model, not a neural network trained in epochs. Predict obtains the attack probability before learn updates the model. HAT has internal ADWIN detectors for branch adaptation; the separate monitor records changes in observed prediction errors.

Snapshot: 30 lines; SHA256 6110282de738ea0aa149e0181187053dac8c70262b82806d8ddce47011a96b03.

Named operations

- OnlineDetector.__init__ (L7): Constructs the HAT and a separate error ADWIN. Neither object has learned examples yet.

- OnlineDetector.predict (L18): Obtains class probabilities; missing class 1 defaults to zero. Thresholding creates a binary prediction and elapsed time measures prediction only.

- OnlineDetector.learn (L24): Optionally feeds 0/1 prediction error to the external monitor, updates HAT with the ground-truth label, and returns whether the external monitor alarmed.

src/m3/metrics.py

Measurement envelopes and detection metrics. Keeps missing measurements distinct from real zeroes. All quality scores are calculated from scored observations, excluding warm-up and unknown labels. ROC-AUC uses average ranks for equal scores. Exact AUC retains labels and scores in memory, so the entire pipeline is not constant-memory despite incremental model learning.

Snapshot: 92 lines; SHA256 bceece8e984d031c70bfa66a952a7dd661ca08cd830d720dd170006614ee89ec.

Named operations

- measurement (L7): Wraps a value with its unit, evidence status and reason; None or non-finite Python floats become explicitly unavailable.

- roc_auc (L23): Computes rank-based AUC: probability that an attack scores above a benign example, with tied scores receiving half credit. Needs both classes.

- QualityMetrics.__init__ (L41): Initializes confusion counts and raw score/latency lists for one run, plus counters for held-out SYNFlood recall.

- QualityMetrics.update (L49): Adds exactly one scored labeled prediction. Prediction must have happened before this method and before learning.

- QualityMetrics.summary (L58): Calculates attack metrics, per-class metrics, mean/p95 latency, and optional unseen-family recall; division by zero produces unavailable.

src/m3/engine.py

Replay execution and predict-before-learn evaluation. Evaluation is shared by offline replay and live collection. run_replay chooses CSV or PCAP input, maintains counts, obtains independent labels, samples features, and writes evidence. The source field official_5g_nidd records provenance; it does not imply live deployment or a completed study.

Snapshot: 236 lines; SHA256 9e99cd0676d80f647099d2de20f780eaef724480f2af393907a2d21fbc6b21f7.

Named operations

- Evaluation.__init__ (L19): Creates one detector and evaluator state for this run: quality, first attack/alarm, unsampled-packet tracking, processed count, and summary-save timer.

- Evaluation.observe (L31): One observation enters here. Exclude held-out warm-up examples, predict and log first, score labeled evaluation observations, then learn. Unknown labels never train.

- Evaluation.summary (L106): Produces metric envelopes plus detection delay and packet count. CSV row positions cannot supply physical delay. Post-drift recovery remains unavailable pending annotated analysis.

- run_replay (L137): Verifies official input (unless explicitly a fixture), creates a writer/new model, starts resource monitoring, replays CSV or PCAP, then finalizes evidence even for captured processing failures.

- run_replay.observe_window (L185): Assigns truth to a completed packet window, keeps warm-up separate, and calls the shared evaluator with independent original-packet counts when available.

CSV warm-up is determined from eligible records before the selection draw. At N=10, roughly one tenth of that prefix is actually learned. Every selected held-out observation is predicted, scored, then learned; this is online test-then-train with immediate oracle labels, not a frozen held-out model test. The scenario="drift" name alone does not inject a shift. Packet windows derive ground truth from unsampled original packets. The final partial capture window is intentionally dropped.

src/m3/packets.py

Packet decoding and fixed-width window features. Packet stores a small parsed header summary. WindowAccumulator turns sampled packets into packet-window-v1 features. Multiplying a sampled packet by its reported sampling rate estimates traffic volume; it does not recover original packet identities. CSV flow-v1 features are a different schema.

Snapshot: 132 lines; SHA256 b7eef6e17c986b923014416da92e7f07dd381b51cfba5db03705143c8ebbd692.

Named operations

- Packet (L12): Stores arrival/capture time, original frame length, IP protocol, TCP SYN flag, and inverse sampling probability N.

- parse_header (L20): Parses supported Ethernet/VLAN/IPv4/IPv6 headers defensively and derives a SYN flag. Unsupported or too-short input returns None, not guessed fields.

- iter_pcap (L64): Streams pcap/pcapng records, requires Ethernet link type, and rejects timestamps that go backwards.

- WindowAccumulator.__init__ (L85): Validates a positive window width and initializes an unstarted accumulator.

- WindowAccumulator._record (L92): Creates packet-window features from currently stored sampled packets; empty windows get zero numeric features and empty_window=1.

- WindowAccumulator.advance (L111): Emits completed windows up to the new relative-time bin, including empty windows, and rejects backwards or unreasonable gaps.

- WindowAccumulator.add (L126): Closes previous windows before appending the new packet to its time bin. It is a generator; work occurs when iterated.

- WindowAccumulator.finish (L130): Can emit the currently open window. Offline engine intentionally does not call it, avoiding a partially captured final window.

src/m3/ground_truth.py

Conservative packet-to-flow ground truth. Matches original packet headers against verified numeric official flow intervals. Matching uses bidirectional endpoints, ports for TCP/UDP, protocol, and epoch time. Unknown/conflicting cases stay unknown. Ground truth is calculated independently of feature sampling; this prevents discarded attack packets from disappearing from the test answer.

Snapshot: 172 lines; SHA256 0f71ce43cfc297b8a7021adebfeeeb53c0d9b5a797ee87dda55420c1f410327d.

Named operations

- flow_key (L15): Normalizes IP addresses and sorts endpoint pairs, so forward and reverse packets share one lookup key; TCP/UDP need numeric ports.

- packet_key (L27): Builds a flow key from an Ethernet frame using dpkt. Unsupported protocols, noninitial IPv4 fragments, and parse errors return None.

- IntervalIndex.__init__ (L53): Builds sorted interval starts plus a balanced max-end tree to avoid scanning all historical flows for every packet.

- IntervalIndex.at (L65): Uses binary search on starts and max-end pruning to return intervals overlapping the timestamp, allowing one microsecond tolerance.

- FlowLabels.__init__ (L82): Loads/validates the prepared numeric interval table, groups matching endpoints/protocols, and builds an interval index for each group.

- FlowLabels.match (L136): Finds candidate official intervals for one original packet. Zero matches or mixed binary labels return unknown; same binary label with several families becomes mixed_flood.

- WindowTruth.__init__ (L151): Tracks all original packets and authoritative positive families for one window, independently of sampled features.

- WindowTruth.add (L156): Counts each original packet, counts unknown labels, and records positive attack families.

- WindowTruth.label (L162): Any known flood packet makes a positive window; otherwise unknown packets make it unscored; no unknown/positive packets means benign, including empty windows.

src/m3/sflow.py

Bounded binary sFlow v5 decoder. Converts UDP payload bytes exported by OVS into Packet objects. Bounds checks and length-prefixed records prevent reading beyond available bytes. Unsupported sample/record types are skipped by length. This decoder is intentionally narrower than a complete sFlow implementation.

Snapshot: 79 lines; SHA256 b2fc1e1166b1fcaff16081dff2c7fe451294d74d636edc805088487171c836c2.

Named operations

- DecodeError (L8): A ValueError subclass specifically identifying malformed or unsupported sFlow datagrams.

- Reader.__init__ (L13): Retains the byte buffer and a cursor starting at zero.

- Reader.take (L16): Checks that a read stays in bounds, slices exactly size bytes, advances the cursor, and returns the bytes.

- Reader.integer (L23): Reads four bytes as one unsigned big-endian 32-bit integer.

- Reader.record (L26): Reads tag and length, extracts the body, skips 4-byte alignment padding, and returns tag/body.

- decode_datagram (L33): Checks sFlow v5 framing, walks compact/expanded flow samples and raw packet records, and returns supported parsed packets plus agent health metadata.

src/m3/live.py

Live UDP collector. Binds a UDP socket, saves raw received sFlow datagrams, decodes sampled headers, forms windows, and invokes Evaluation. It does not sample again after OVS sampling. Labels come from separately supplied LabelTimeline annotations; immediate online training requires those experimental labels.

Snapshot: 112 lines; SHA256 38699a758a1d423919d38e69e4f2bbb3acac6bba2627179c0e13e8a852225de7.

Named operations

- run_live (L14): Creates a UDP collector for live_sflow only, captures raw payloads and health counts, forms windows by receipt time, evaluates them, and finalizes on success or failure.

- run_live.observe (L38): Looks up a full-window annotation and sends the labeled window, sampled count, warm-up flag and actual relative observation time to Evaluation.

Live time is collector receipt/wall-clock time rather than original packet capture time. Raw frame matching is not performed in this collector: it uses LabelTimeline. It cannot claim independently counted original packets-to-detect from received samples alone. No input trace is replayed by this function; SDN orchestration creates traffic separately.

src/m3/resources.py

Background process/resource measurement. Samples collector/detector process CPU and RSS about once per second, optionally samples a separate controller PID, and delegates switch/OpenFlow observations to LabMeasurements. CPU percent uses one logical CPU as 100%; it may exceed 100 for a multithreaded process.

Snapshot: 91 lines; SHA256 456ff4f6423e070466508aeec620a03ae86f2520d1c258f19d79d4075e2ad73e.

Named operations

- ResourceMonitor.__init__ (L13): Binds this process and optional controller process, constructs lab observers, and prepares a daemon thread and stop event.

- ResourceMonitor.start (L27): Starts independent lab collection, primes CPU counters, then starts the background loop.

- ResourceMonitor.sample (L35): Takes one process/controller resource snapshot, asks OVS for entries, retains it and appends it to resources.csv.

- ResourceMonitor._loop (L53): Waits one second at a time on a stop event; samples until stopping is requested.

src/m3/lab.py

Independent lab observations. Reads OVS flow-table snapshots and captures loopback OpenFlow traffic with tcpdump in Linux. These are separate observations from received sFlow bytes. The subprocess argument lists are explicit; no shell command string is assembled from bridge names.

Snapshot: 103 lines; SHA256 eef3df4094748f83ca5f3876c7e03d12e7cd05660c62267405d84ea918f19c08.

Named operations

- LabMeasurements.__init__ (L13): Enables OVS/OpenFlow observations only for a configured live run; initializes unavailable reasons for unconfigured measurements.

- LabMeasurements.start (L24): Starts tcpdump on Linux loopback for the configured OpenFlow TCP port and preserves its diagnostics.

- LabMeasurements.sample (L53): Runs a read-only ovs-ofctl flow dump with a one-second timeout and counts flow-entry lines; errors yield unavailable.

- LabMeasurements.finish (L73): Stops tcpdump cleanly, reads captured frame bytes, releases resources, then returns independent OpenFlow bandwidth and mean OVS entries.

src/m3/provenance.py

Data identity and checksum checks. Hashes files in chunks and checks their identity against the official dataset manifest. Matching a local manifest is necessary for these runs; the upstream download/checksum verification in scripts/fetch_dataset.py is what establishes how manifest entries were produced.

Snapshot: 33 lines; SHA256 06bb4a015d87b6ea526f4bc195c695efb1d9468dcaf7501fc8ded2c28989e41e.

- sha256 (L8): Hashes a file incrementally in one-MiB chunks; the digest is a fingerprint of exact bytes.

- verify_input (L16): Checks official manifest identity, per-file verification status and actual SHA256. Unknown, unverified or modified files are rejected.

src/m3/store.py

Evidence writer and read-only run repository. RunWriter creates a unique directory, appends raw CSV evidence, and replaces JSON summaries atomically. RunRepository reads the summaries and a limited series for the dashboard. It validates run IDs and rejects run-directory symlinks. The API series is a visualization sample, not the data from which experimental metrics should be recalculated.

Snapshot: 182 lines; SHA256 1d6e7674d40e71c71b04c96850503b2feccc8abd4c06509f2674c4524ca6836d.

Named operations

- utc_now (L13): Returns an ISO 8601 UTC time string for run bookkeeping, independent of client timezone.

- dependency_versions (L17): Reads installed package versions for reproducibility; missing distributions are recorded explicitly.

- atomic_json (L27): Writes valid JSON to a sibling temporary path, then replaces the visible target so readers avoid a partially written JSON document.

- RunWriter.__init__ (L34): Creates a UUID-named run directory, raw CSV files with fixed schemas, and an initial running summary with model/config/data provenance.

- RunWriter.append (L102): Uses a lock to append and immediately flush one raw CSV row; this is raw evidence, not dashboard formatting.

- RunWriter.save (L107): Uses the same lock to atomically replace the run JSON summary.

- RunWriter.finish (L111): Marks status/error/end time, saves final metrics, then closes raw evidence streams.

- RunRepository.__init__ (L125): Resolves the configured evidence root to an absolute filesystem location.

- RunRepository.directory (L128): Allows only a 32-character lowercase-hex run ID and a real nonsymlink run directory beneath the evidence root.

- RunRepository.get (L136): Loads the chosen run_summary.json through the checked directory lookup.

- RunRepository.list (L139): Finds valid readable run summaries and sorts newest first; absent roots return an empty list, in-progress unreadable files are skipped.

- RunRepository.series (L151): Counts CSV records, chooses evenly spaced row indices if needed, rereads selected rows and converts values for JSON using bounded result memory.

CSV series first scans to count rows and then scans again; memory is bounded by the selected result size, but work still grows with file length. Uniform series downsampling can omit brief spikes or drift events. Atomic replacement protects readers against partial JSON; it does not provide a full database transaction or fsync guarantee.

src/m3/analysis.py

Comparable-trial aggregation and Pareto charts. Groups matching evidence/settings, summarizes repeated trials, and plots quality/cost. It filters fixture and incomplete runs from aggregation while preserving failed-run information. Pareto-efficient means no other point is at least as accurate and at most as costly with one strict improvement. This module does not automatically choose a knee point or prove the required full experiment matrix is complete.

Snapshot: 234 lines; SHA256 b6117bd3a5df59fb84a18684c7a8022227921d4ce7bbb2debde89005bd361f2b.

Named operations

- comparison_key (L22): Serializes source/mode/unit/scenario/schema/checksum/model settings into a stable key so incompatible runs do not get averaged together.

- pareto (L37): Keeps a point unless another has at least its F1 and no more cost, with one strict improvement. Exact ties are both retained.

- aggregate (L51): Groups completed nonfixture runs by comparison key and N, calculates metric mean/sample standard deviation/min/max, and retains reasons and actual valid counts.

- analyse (L88): Loads runs, saves aggregates and failures, produces headless plots, and exports measured-bandwidth Pareto fronts. No automatic knee-point selector is implemented here.

A sampling sweep is not automatically a valid finished study: inspect actual trial counts, distinct seeds, source, settings and scenarios. The key does not include every possible label annotation or software revision, so verify those manually before comparing. front is the set of nondominated points; selecting an operational knee still needs an agreed rule and independent verification.

src/m3/api.py

Read-only HTTP results interface. FastAPI exposes saved runs and timelines to the browser. The HTTP server does not train the model, start sweeps, or perform live collection. The process running m3 run/live writes evidence; the separate m3 serve process reads it.

Snapshot: 64 lines; SHA256 5caf834a79dc8eb42075c91aa790e387a1f8420cedf712d73b89b9d6bb17ef9b.

Named operations

- create_app (L9): Builds a read-only FastAPI app with local development CORS, an evidence repository, API routes, and an optional static dashboard mount.

- create_app.health (L20): Simple service/schema health response; does not inspect model accuracy or completeness of evidence.

- create_app.runs (L24): Returns the repository run list, including status and source distinctions.

- create_app.overview (L28): Counts statuses and reports the maximum F1 among completed runs; this endpoint does not enforce scientific comparability for best_run_id.

- create_app.run (L42): Returns one summary, converting invalid/missing run directory errors to HTTP 404.

- create_app.series (L49): Returns sampled visualization series for one run; FastAPI validates the limit between 2 and 10,000.

Path indexing example: for Project/src/m3/api.py, parents[0] is m3, parents[1] is src and parents[2] is Project. The optional static mount therefore correctly targets project-root frontend/dist, and is enabled only when that build directory exists. best_run_id in overview is a raw maximum across completed runs; it is not a fair cross-scenario ranking.

SDN and dataset tools: every source line explained

This guide covers the nine files listed below exactly as inspected in the working tree. Each physical source line has one numbered table row, including blank lines and closing punctuation. Source is reproduced beside its explanation so that line numbers remain meaningful even if the application later changes. These are explanations of implementation, not claims that network experiments were run during guide creation.

How these files fit together

1. fetch_dataset.py obtains and verifies official bytes; its manifest provides file lineage.

2. inspect_session_labels.py checks whether CSV tuples have conflicting classes. This is an audit, not packet labeling.

3. prepare_flow_labels.py joins official labels to numerical Argus flow intervals using exact record offsets.

4. setup_sdn.sh provisions Linux dependencies and preflight.py checks them.

5. controller.py supplies learning-switch forwarding; topology.py creates a separate virtual testbed with real OVS sFlow.

6. validate_sflow.py checks received telemetry bytes at two sampling rates. run_live_validation.py checks the actual M3 collector against benign telemetry.

A publisher checksum proves that a file matches the publisher's advertised bytes. It does not prove a label is scientifically correct. A successful CSV/Argus join proves record correspondence under the checks implemented here. It does not prove every PCAP packet has an unambiguous label. Live benign telemetry proves that the collection path runs. It does not measure attack detection quality.

Syntax used repeatedly

with closes files/sockets after a block, even on errors. try/finally arranges cleanup. subprocess.Popen starts a child asynchronously; subprocess.run waits. A subprocess argument list passes each argument separately rather than composing a shell command. poll() is None means a process is still running. time.monotonic() is for elapsed deadlines; time.time() is wall-clock epoch time. Python indentation defines blocks. A trailing comma is allowed in multiline calls and containers.

scripts/fetch_dataset.py

Downloads selected official 5G-NIDD release files from Fairdata/Etsin, verifies publisher size/SHA256, extracts selected ZIP members, and writes provenance in data/manifest.json. Uses Python standard-library modules only and network access to the publisher. It does not clean training data, train a model, establish chronological ordering, or label packets.

scripts/setup_sdn.sh

Provisions a Linux/Ubuntu or WSL SDN environment. Requires root, package-network access and a Linux service environment; installs OVS, Mininet, capture/replay and Argus tooling, a project-local uv, Python 3.12, and the editable project. This installer changes the system and executes a downloaded uv installer. The guide explains it without executing it.

3set -euo pipefailAbort on failing commands, undefined variables, or failing pipeline stages.
4project_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"Find this script's directory via BASH_SOURCE[0], move one parent up, and store its absolute working path; quoting preserves spaces.
5if [[ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]]; thenCompare numeric user ID with root's ID 0.
6 echo 'Run this installer with sudo inside Ubuntu.' >&2Print the sudo requirement to standard error using >&2.
7 exit 1Return failure exit status 1.
8fiClose the root-check conditional.
9apt-get updateRefresh Ubuntu's package index; this modifies the Linux environment.
10apt-get install -y openvswitch-switch mininet iproute2 iputils-ping tcpdump tcpreplay curl python3-venv argus-clientInstall OVS switching, Mininet emulation, network/ping tools, packet capture/replay tools, curl, virtual environments, and the Argus reader.
11if [[ ! -x "$project_root/.tools/uv" ]]; thenTest whether the project-local uv executable is missing or not executable.
12 curl --fail --location https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | env UV_INSTALL_DIR="$project_root/.tools" UV_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 shDownload and execute Astral's installer; environment settings place uv under .tools and prevent shell PATH modification. This line executes downloaded code.
13fiClose the uv-install conditional.
14sdn_env="${M3_SDN_ENV:-/opt/m3-sdn}"Choose M3_SDN_ENV when set and nonempty; otherwise use /opt/m3-sdn.
15"$project_root/.tools/uv" python install 3.12Ask uv to install/manage Python 3.12.
16if [[ ! -x "$sdn_env/bin/python" ]]; thenCheck whether the selected virtual environment already has an executable Python.
17 "$project_root/.tools/uv" venv --python 3.12 "$sdn_env"Create that virtual environment with Python 3.12.
18fiClose the environment-creation conditional.
19"$project_root/.tools/uv" pip install --python "$sdn_env/bin/python" \Start installing packages into the selected Python; trailing backslash continues the shell command.
20 'os-ken==3.1.1' 'setuptools<81' 'mininet==2.3.0.dev6'Pin OS-Ken 3.1.1 and Mininet 2.3.0.dev6, and constrain setuptools below 81 for compatibility.
21"$project_root/.tools/uv" pip install --python "$sdn_env/bin/python" -e "$project_root"Install this repository in editable mode, so its Python source changes are used without reinstalling it.
22service openvswitch-switch startStart the Open vSwitch service.
23"$sdn_env/bin/python" "$project_root/sdn/preflight.py"Run prerequisite checks with the SDN environment's Python; its exit code becomes this script's final status.

sdn/controller.py

OS-Ken Ethernet learning-switch application. Requires the OS-Ken environment and an OpenFlow 1.3 switch. On switch connection, installs a table-miss rule; on unknown destinations, floods; on known destinations, installs a 30-second-idle learned rule. M3 and the attack labels do not enter forwarding rules. There is no attack-blocking or mitigation logic in this file.

sdn/inspect_session_labels.py

Audits official CSV tuples before considering packet-label matching. Uses standard-library CSV, local service lookup and JSON. Produces one JSON report per input CSV, including conflicting labels and unsupported rows. It canonicalizes TCP/UDP direction and audits ICMP only by endpoint pair. It never asserts that a conflict-free tuple proves complete packet ground truth.

4ICMP is audited by endpoint pair only because Argus pseudo-port semantics mustDocument that ICMP is grouped only by endpoint addresses.
5be verified before packet matching. Unknown protocols/ports remain unjoined.Warn that unsupported ports/protocols remain outside tuple matching.

sdn/prepare_flow_labels.py

Uses verified official BS2 CSV and Argus sources to create flow-interval labels with epoch times, endpoints and binary labels. Requires Ubuntu Argus ra, previously fetched CSV and Argus archives, and data/manifest.json. Exact Offset identity, endpoint/protocol/count comparisons and duration/displayed-time consistency establish the join. Output consists of retained ra export, normalized flow labels, a JSON join audit and updated/checkpointed provenance. It does not establish capture packet coverage by itself.

sdn/topology.py

Creates four Mininet hosts connected through a named OVS bridge to an external controller. Configures real switch-side sFlow, checks connectivity, optionally generates benign ICMP or replays a prepared Ethernet PCAP, saves evidence and cleans up. Requires Linux privileges and SDN tools. No physical uplink is added. Replay requires externally documented Ethernet/address mapping and separately supplied ground truth.

sdn/validate_sflow.py

Runs a simple UDP receiver and benign topology twice, at N=1 and N=10, to check controller connectivity and actual OVS sFlow export. Requires the Linux SDN environment. Saves raw datagrams as hexadecimal, per-N topology evidence/logs and validation.json. Its small parser counts sample containers; it does not reconstruct features, run M3, validate packet labels or prove sampling effectiveness quantitatively.

18def flow_sample_count(payload):Define a small top-level sFlow flow-sample counter, not a complete sFlow decoder.
19 if len(payload) < 28 or struct.unpack_from("!I", payload)[0] != 5:Require at least 28 bytes and sFlow version 5; !I means one unsigned 32-bit big-endian integer.
20 return 0Count zero for a too-short/non-v5 datagram.
21 kind = struct.unpack_from("!I", payload, 4)[0]Read agent-address type from byte offset four.
22 if kind not in (1, 2):Support only IPv4 type one and IPv6 type two.
23 return 0Count zero for unsupported address types.
24 offset = 12 if kind == 1 else 24Choose header offset after the IPv4 or IPv6 agent address.
25 if len(payload) < offset + 16:Require enough bytes for subagent, sequence, uptime and sample count.
26 return 0Count zero for truncated header.
27 count = struct.unpack_from("!I", payload, offset + 12)[0]Read number of top-level samples twelve bytes into this header section.
28 offset += 16Advance past its 16-byte fixed portion.
29 flows = 0Initialize flow-sample count.
30 for _ in range(count):Visit the advertised number of sample records.
31 if len(payload) < offset + 8:Require at least the next sample's tag and length header.
32 breakStop if this outer header is truncated.
33 tag, length = struct.unpack_from("!II", payload, offset)Decode two unsigned big-endian integers: sample tag and body length.
34 flows += int(tag in (1, 3))Count ordinary flow sample tag one or expanded flow sample tag three; other sample kinds do not increment.
35 offset += 8 + lengthSkip the eight-byte sample header plus advertised body; payload length and inner content are not validated here.
36 return flowsReturn the count observed by this lightweight diagnostic.

Questions you should be able to answer after reading

- Why do raw downloads need a publisher hash while extracted members also need parent hashes?

- Why is an Offset join stronger than guessing labels from capture filenames?

- Why does joining an ICMP endpoint pair require care about overlapping flow intervals and packet coverage?

- Why is controller forwarding independent of M3's ground truth and predictions here?

- Which script counts sFlow containers and which launches the actual M3 collector?

- Why can an unlabeled benign live run demonstrate telemetry collection without demonstrating attack recall?

- Why is received UDP payload size different from complete network bandwidth or controller control-channel traffic?

Implementation boundaries and observations

These files support several different evidence levels. Keep publisher download verification, flow-record join verification, packet ground-truth verification, and live attack-quality evaluation separate in your explanation and report.

The downloader refuses to overwrite mismatching originals and partial files. It verifies member contents before reusing extracted files and rejects paths that escape the extraction directory. Its signed-URL hostname check happens before opening the URL; redirects are not independently host-restricted. The manifest writes stage a file before replacement but provide no general concurrent-writer lock.

The strict flow-label preparation currently targets BS2 sessions for UDPFlood, SYNFlood and ICMPFlood. It requires the separately downloaded per-session Argus inputs. It compares addresses, protocol, packet/byte counts, duration and displayed times; it does not compare source/destination ports to the CSV ports. Displayed-time validation checks minute/second distance within an hour, whereas the saved epoch times come from Argus. A manifest entry matching path/digest is required, but verify_source does not explicitly test its verification_status. These describe the actual checks without changing them.

The lightweight sFlow diagnostic checks version, agent-address type and outer sample headers. It does not comprehensively validate nested record lengths. Passing diagnostics requires received flow samples for both rates, not a proven 10:1 ratio, detection accuracy or learned adaptation.

The live collector validation has no labels path. Ground truth cannot be obtained from the model's own predictions. Labeled online test-then-train learning, drift-error signals and accuracy require a valid external label source elsewhere in the application.

Topology setup removes the existing fixed-name m3s1 bridge, creates a local testbed, and stops it afterward. Timed orchestration uses real delays and bounded process waits. Some timeout paths have no force-kill fallback. Nothing here was executed to create this guide; source inspection and line-coverage verification were the checks performed.

Frontend: source and line-by-line explanation

This guide follows the current checked-out frontend source. Line numbers restart for each file and refer to physical source lines, including blank lines. Each file has a complete original source listing and a numbered explanation table. Application files were not changed.

What the frontend currently does

The current UI is M3 Observatory, a read-only M3 experiment dashboard. The proposed unified M1/M2/M3 screen is not currently implemented here. This UI displays saved evidence; it has no controls for training, starting experiments, or collecting telemetry.

The browser loads index.html → main.tsx → App. App asks api.ts for /api/runs and /api/overview, chooses a run, then requests that run's summary and /series?limit=1000. api.ts validates JSON. evidence.ts formats metrics and groups comparable trials. App draws SVG charts and HTML tables. style.css controls layout. In development, Vite forwards /api to FastAPI on port 8000.

Auto-refresh schedules the next request 3 seconds after the previous one completes. Manual Refresh restarts reads. The frontend does not calculate model predictions or reconstruct missing measurements.

Syntax to recognize

- const prevents binding reassignment; objects bound with const can still change. let permits reassignment.

- (x) => ... is an arrow function. map transforms array items; filter retains them; some asks whether any match.

- ... spreads object/array members. {name} can destructure fields; JSX braces evaluate JavaScript.

- Type annotations, interfaces, casts, type imports, and non-null ! assertions aid TypeScript checking and disappear at runtime. They do not validate JSON.

- ?. safely accesses a nullable object. ?? defaults null/undefined; || defaults any falsy value. condition ? a : b selects one expression.

- JSX becomes React operations. className selects CSS styling; htmlFor links labels; onChange and onClick receive callbacks.

- useState stores [value,setter]; setters rerender. useEffect handles external work and cleanup; useMemo caches derived values; useCallback caches a function.

- async functions return promises; await reads their eventual result. Promise.all awaits requests together. try/catch/finally handles success, failure, and always-run work.

- Tests use expect for assertions and vi.fn for mocks; resolved/rejected mock values simulate successful/failed asynchronous requests.

frontend/src/api.ts

Read-only HTTP boundary. Fetches FastAPI routes and rejects malformed supported-contract responses before components display them.

Complete source

import type { RunSummary, Series, Overview } from './types';

function record(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

export function validateRun(value: unknown): RunSummary {
  if (!record(value) || value.schema_version !== 1 || typeof value.run_id !== 'string' ||
      typeof value.source !== 'string' || !['csv_replay', 'pcap_replay', 'live_sflow'].includes(String(value.mode)) ||
      !['running', 'completed', 'failed'].includes(String(value.status)) ||
      typeof value.sampling_rate !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(value.sampling_rate) || value.sampling_rate < 1 ||
      !['flow', 'window'].includes(String(value.unit)) || typeof value.scenario !== 'string' ||
      typeof value.seed !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value.seed) ||
      typeof value.created_at !== 'string' || typeof value.drift_count !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value.drift_count) ||
      !(value.ended_at === null || typeof value.ended_at === 'string') ||
      !(value.error === null || typeof value.error === 'string') ||
      !record(value.counts) || !record(value.metrics) || !record(value.config)) {
    throw new Error('The server returned an unsupported run format. Expected result schema version 1.');
  }
  for (const key of ['input', 'sampled', 'evaluated', 'warmup', 'excluded', 'unlabeled']) {
    if (typeof value.counts[key] !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value.counts[key]) || Number(value.counts[key]) < 0) {
      throw new Error('The server returned invalid run counts.');
    }
  }
  for (const metric of Object.values(value.metrics)) {
    if (!record(metric) || !['measured', 'estimated', 'unavailable'].includes(String(metric.status)) ||
        !(metric.value === null || (typeof metric.value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(metric.value))) ||
        typeof metric.unit !== 'string' || !(metric.reason === null || typeof metric.reason === 'string')) throw new Error('The server returned invalid metric evidence.');
  }
  return value as unknown as RunSummary;
}

async function get(path: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<unknown> {
  const response = await fetch(path, { signal, headers: { Accept: 'application/json' } });
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Could not load experiment evidence (HTTP ${response.status}).`);
  try { return await response.json(); } catch { throw new Error('The experiment server did not return JSON.'); }
}

export async function getRuns(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<RunSummary[]> {
  const data = await get('/api/runs', signal);
  if (!record(data) || !Array.isArray(data.runs)) throw new Error('The server returned an invalid run list.');
  return data.runs.map(validateRun);
}
export async function getRun(id: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<RunSummary> {
  return validateRun(await get(`/api/runs/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, signal));
}
export async function getSeries(id: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Series> {
  const data = await get(`/api/runs/${encodeURIComponent(id)}/series?limit=1000`, signal);
  if (!record(data) || !Array.isArray(data.predictions) || !Array.isArray(data.resources) || !Array.isArray(data.drift)) {
    throw new Error('The server returned invalid timeline evidence.');
  }
  for (const point of data.predictions) {
    if (!record(point) || typeof point.index !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(point.index) ||
        !(point.score === null || (typeof point.score === 'number' && Number.isFinite(point.score) && point.score >= 0 && point.score <= 1)) ||
        ![0, 1, true, false, null].includes(point.y_true as number | boolean | null) ||
        !(typeof point.time === 'string' || (typeof point.time === 'number' && Number.isFinite(point.time)))) {
      throw new Error('The server returned an invalid prediction.');
    }
  }
  for (const event of data.drift) {
    if (!record(event) || typeof event.index !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(event.index) ||
        typeof event.event !== 'string' || typeof event.detector !== 'string' ||
        !(typeof event.time === 'string' || (typeof event.time === 'number' && Number.isFinite(event.time)))) {
      throw new Error('The server returned an invalid drift event.');
    }
  }
  return data as unknown as Series;
}
export async function getOverview(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Overview> {
  const data = await get('/api/overview', signal);
  if (!record(data) || !['total_runs', 'completed_runs', 'running_runs', 'failed_runs'].every(key =>
    typeof data[key] === 'number' && Number.isFinite(data[key]) && Number(data[key]) >= 0)) {
    throw new Error('The server returned an invalid experiment overview.');
  }
  return data as unknown as Overview;
}

63 !(typeof event.time === 'string' || (typeof event.time === 'number' && Number.isFinite(event.time)))) {Allows event time as a string or finite number.

70 const data = await get('/api/overview', signal);Requests /api/overview.
71 if (!record(data) || !['total_runs', 'completed_runs', 'running_runs', 'failed_runs'].every(key =>Requires an object and begins checking all four known run counters.

Validation boundaries

These checks validate a supported response shape; they do not prove the experiment was scientifically correct. Run validation does not parse timestamp strings, enforce every counter is an integer, verify cross-field count relationships, or validate provenance. Series validation checks arrays and several prediction/drift fields, but does not validate each resource element or every Prediction field. Compile-time casts do not add missing runtime checks.

frontend/src/evidence.ts

Pure evidence helpers. Formats values, separates comparison groups, and identifies measured Pareto-efficient trials without requests.

Complete source

import type { Metric, RunSummary } from './types';

const ratioKeys = new Set(['precision', 'recall', 'f1', 'roc_auc', 'false_positive_rate', 'unseen_attack_recall']);
export function metricValue(metric: Metric | undefined): number | null {
  return metric && metric.status !== 'unavailable' && typeof metric.value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(metric.value)
    ? metric.value : null;
}
export function formatMetric(key: string, metric: Metric | undefined): string {
  const value = metricValue(metric);
  if (value === null) return 'Unavailable';
  if (ratioKeys.has(key)) return `${(value * 100).toFixed(1)}%`;
  return `${new Intl.NumberFormat('en', { maximumFractionDigits: 2 }).format(value)}${metric?.unit ? ` ${metric.unit}` : ''}`;
}
export function sourceName(source: string) {
  return source === 'official_5g_nidd' ? 'Official 5G-NIDD' : source === 'fixture' ? 'Development fixture' : source === 'live_sflow' ? 'Live telemetry' : source.replaceAll('_', ' ');
}
export function modeName(mode: RunSummary['mode']) {
  return { csv_replay: 'CSV flow replay', pcap_replay: 'Packet capture replay', live_sflow: 'Live sFlow' }[mode];
}
export function compatibleRuns(runs: RunSummary[], selected: RunSummary): RunSummary[] {
  const settings = ['threshold', 'grace_period', 'drift_delta', 'window_seconds', 'warmup_records', 'warmup_seconds', 'max_records'];
  const signature = (run: RunSummary) => JSON.stringify(settings.map(key => [key, run.config[key] ?? null]));
  return runs.filter(run => run.status === 'completed' && run.source === selected.source && run.mode === selected.mode &&
    run.scenario === selected.scenario && run.unit === selected.unit &&
    run.feature_schema === selected.feature_schema &&
    (run.provenance?.sha256 ?? null) === (selected.provenance?.sha256 ?? null) &&
    signature(run) === signature(selected));
}
export function paretoRuns(runs: RunSummary[], costKey: string): Set<string> {
  const measured = runs.filter(run => run.metrics.f1?.status === 'measured' && run.metrics[costKey]?.status === 'measured' &&
    metricValue(run.metrics.f1) !== null && metricValue(run.metrics[costKey]) !== null);
  return new Set(measured.filter(run => !measured.some(other => {
    const q = metricValue(run.metrics.f1)!; const c = metricValue(run.metrics[costKey])!;
    const oq = metricValue(other.metrics.f1)!; const oc = metricValue(other.metrics[costKey])!;
    return oq >= q && oc <= c && (oq > q || oc < c);
  })).map(run => run.run_id));
}

33 const q = metricValue(run.metrics.f1)!; const c = metricValue(run.metrics[costKey])!;Reads the candidate run's F1 q and resource cost c; ! asserts non-null after filtering.
34 const oq = metricValue(other.metrics.f1)!; const oc = metricValue(other.metrics[costKey])!;Reads the competitor's F1 and resource cost.

36 })).map(run => run.run_id));Maps remaining runs to IDs and constructs a Set for constant-time UI membership tests. This identifies a frontier, not a knee point.
37}Closes the current function, interface, or control block begun above.

Worked comparison example

A has F1 .80 and cost 10; B has F1 .85 and cost 5; C has F1 .70 and cost 2. B dominates A because quality improves and cost falls. B and C are both Pareto-efficient because C is cheaper but less accurate. That frontier does not itself choose a knee point.

compatibleRuns compares a listed set of settings, not every possible config field. Missing checksums/schema identifiers can compare equal. Experiment producers still need to record correct provenance.

frontend/src/App.tsx

Main M3 dashboard and its chart/card components. Owns polling, selection, errors, and rendering saved evidence.

Complete source

import { useCallback, useEffect, useMemo, useState } from 'react';
import { getOverview, getRun, getRuns, getSeries } from './api';
import { compatibleRuns, formatMetric, metricValue, modeName, paretoRuns, sourceName } from './evidence';
import type { Metric, Overview, RunSummary, Series } from './types';

const POLL_MS = 3000;
const emptySeries: Series = { predictions: [], resources: [], drift: [] };
const number = (value: number) => value.toLocaleString('en');
const timeLabel = (value: number | string) => typeof value === 'number' ? `${value.toFixed(2)} s` : value;
const dateLabel = (value: string) => {
  const date = new Date(value);
  return Number.isNaN(date.valueOf()) ? value : date.toLocaleString(undefined, { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
};

function Badge({ children, tone = '' }: { children: React.ReactNode; tone?: string }) {
  return <span className={`badge ${tone}`}>{children}</span>;
}

function MetricCard({ name, metricKey, metric, caption }: { name: string; metricKey: string; metric?: Metric; caption: string }) {
  const missing = metricValue(metric) === null;
  return <article className={`metric-card ${missing ? 'metric-missing' : ''}`}>
    <div className="metric-label">{name}<span className="metric-symbol" aria-hidden="true">↗</span></div>
    <div className="metric-value">{formatMetric(metricKey, metric)}</div>
    <p>{missing ? metric?.reason || 'No measurement saved for this run.' : caption}</p>
    <span className={`evidence-tag ${metric?.status || 'unavailable'}`}>{missing ? 'unavailable' : metric?.status}</span>
  </article>;
}

function Timeline({ series, unit, threshold }: { series: Series; unit: string; threshold: number }) {
  const points = series.predictions;
  if (!points.length) return <div className="chart-empty"><span className="empty-glyph" aria-hidden="true">⌁</span><h3>No predictions recorded yet</h3><p>This panel will show detection probabilities and ground truth when the run saves evaluated observations.</p></div>;
  const width = 840, height = 240, left = 45, right = 20, top = 15, bottom = 40;
  const min = Math.min(...points.map(p => p.index)), max = Math.max(...points.map(p => p.index));
  const x = (i: number) => left + ((i - min) / Math.max(1, max - min)) * (width - left - right);
  const y = (score: number) => top + (1 - Math.min(1, Math.max(0, score))) * (height - top - bottom);
  let penDown = false;
  const path = points.map(point => {
    if (point.score === null) { penDown = false; return ''; }
    const command = penDown ? 'L' : 'M'; penDown = true;
    return `${command}${x(point.index).toFixed(2)},${y(point.score).toFixed(2)}`;
  }).join(' ');
  const attackCount = points.filter(p => p.y_true === 1 || p.y_true === true).length;
  return <>
    <div className="chart-legend"><span><i className="legend-line" />Attack probability</span><span><i className="legend-dot attack" />Attack ground truth</span><span><i className="legend-dot benign" />Benign ground truth</span><span><i className="legend-line drift" />Drift alarm</span></div>
    <svg className="timeline-svg" viewBox={`0 0 ${width} ${height}`} role="img" aria-label={`Prediction timeline with ${points.length} ${unit} observations, ${attackCount} attack labels, and ${series.drift.length} drift events.`}>
      {[0, .25, .5, .75, 1].map(tick => <g key={tick}><line className="grid-line" x1={left} y1={y(tick)} x2={width - right} y2={y(tick)} /><text className="axis-label" x={left - 12} y={y(tick) + 4} textAnchor="end">{tick.toFixed(2)}</text></g>)}
      <line className="threshold-line" x1={left} y1={y(threshold)} x2={width - right} y2={y(threshold)} />
      {points.filter(p => p.y_true !== null).map(p => <circle key={p.index} cx={x(p.index)} cy={y(p.y_true === 1 || p.y_true === true ? 1 : 0)} r="2.3" className={p.y_true === 1 || p.y_true === true ? 'truth-attack' : 'truth-benign'}><title>{`Observation ${p.index}: ${p.attack_family || (p.y_true ? 'attack' : 'benign')}; ${p.phase}; ${timeLabel(p.time)}`}</title></circle>)}
      {series.drift.filter(d => d.index >= min && d.index <= max).map((d, i) => <line key={i} className="drift-line" x1={x(d.index)} y1={top} x2={x(d.index)} y2={height - bottom}><title>{`${d.detector}: ${d.event} at ${d.index}`}</title></line>)}
      <path d={path} className="probability-line" />
      {[0, .25, .5, .75, 1].map(t => <text key={t} className="axis-label" x={x(min + t * (max - min))} y={height - bottom + 22} textAnchor="middle">{Math.round(min + t * (max - min))}</text>)}
      <text className="axis-title" x={width / 2} y={height - 2} textAnchor="middle">{unit === 'flow' ? 'Flow' : 'Window'} observation index</text>
    </svg>
    <p className="chart-note">Up to 1,000 observations, spread across long runs. Dashed line: decision threshold {threshold}. Warm-up and unlabeled records may appear in this timeline; reported quality metrics use evaluated labels only.</p>
  </>;
}

function Tradeoff({ runs, selectedId }: { runs: RunSummary[]; selectedId: string }) {
  const [costKey, setCostKey] = useState(() => runs.some(run =>
    run.metrics.telemetry_bandwidth_kbps?.status === 'measured' && metricValue(run.metrics.telemetry_bandwidth_kbps) !== null)
    ? 'telemetry_bandwidth_kbps' : 'cpu_percent_mean');
  const frontier = useMemo(() => paretoRuns(runs, costKey), [runs, costKey]);
  const available = runs.filter(run => run.metrics.f1?.status === 'measured' && run.metrics[costKey]?.status === 'measured' && metricValue(run.metrics.f1) !== null && metricValue(run.metrics[costKey]) !== null);
  const costName = costKey === 'telemetry_bandwidth_kbps' ? 'Telemetry bandwidth (kbit/s)' : 'Detector CPU (%)';
  const w = 480, h = 240, left = 55, right = 30, top = 20, bottom = 45;
  const maxCost = Math.max(1, ...available.map(run => metricValue(run.metrics[costKey])!)) * 1.1;
  const x = (c: number) => left + c / maxCost * (w - left - right);
  const y = (q: number) => top + (1 - q) * (h - top - bottom);
  return <>
    <label className="inline-control" htmlFor="cost-axis">Overhead measure<select id="cost-axis" value={costKey} onChange={e => setCostKey(e.target.value)}><option value="telemetry_bandwidth_kbps">Telemetry bandwidth</option><option value="cpu_percent_mean">Detector CPU</option></select></label>
    {available.length ? <>
      <svg className="tradeoff-svg" viewBox={`0 0 ${w} ${h}`} role="img" aria-label={`${available.length} compatible measured trials comparing F1 and ${costName}. ${frontier.size} Pareto-efficient trials.`}>
        {[0, .25, .5, .75, 1].map(q => <g key={q}><line className="grid-line" x1={left} y1={y(q)} x2={w - right} y2={y(q)} /><text className="axis-label" x={left - 10} y={y(q) + 4} textAnchor="end">{Math.round(q * 100)}%</text></g>)}
        {[0, .5, 1].map(c => <text key={c} className="axis-label" x={x(c * maxCost)} y={h - bottom + 20} textAnchor="middle">{(c * maxCost).toFixed(1)}</text>)}
        {available.map(run => <g key={run.run_id}><circle cx={x(metricValue(run.metrics[costKey])!)} cy={y(metricValue(run.metrics.f1)!)} r={run.run_id === selectedId ? 7 : 5} className={frontier.has(run.run_id) ? 'pareto-point' : 'comparison-point'}><title>{`${run.run_id}: N=${run.sampling_rate}, F1 ${formatMetric('f1', run.metrics.f1)}, cost ${formatMetric(costKey, run.metrics[costKey])}${frontier.has(run.run_id) ? ', Pareto efficient' : ''}`}</title></circle><text className="point-label" x={x(metricValue(run.metrics[costKey])!) + 9} y={y(metricValue(run.metrics.f1)!) - 7}>N={run.sampling_rate}</text></g>)}
        <text className="axis-title" x={w / 2} y={h - 4} textAnchor="middle">{costName} · lower is better</text>
      </svg>
      <div className="chart-legend"><span><i className="legend-dot pareto" />Pareto efficient</span><span><i className="legend-dot comparison" />Other measured trials</span></div>
    </> : <div className="chart-empty compact"><h3>Trade-off evidence pending</h3><p>At least one completed trial with measured F1 and {costName.toLowerCase()} is required.</p></div>}
    <p className="chart-note">Only completed trials matching this run's source, mode, scenario, feature schema, dataset checksum, and model settings are compared. Estimated or unavailable costs are excluded.</p>
  </>;
}

const detailMetrics: [string, string][] = [
  ['roc_auc', 'ROC-AUC'], ['false_positive_rate', 'False-positive rate'], ['detection_time_seconds', 'Detection time'],
  ['packets_to_detect', 'Packets to detect'], ['unseen_attack_recall', 'Unseen-attack recall'], ['post_drift_recovery_seconds', 'Post-drift recovery'],
  ['cpu_percent_mean', 'Detector CPU · mean'], ['cpu_percent_p95', 'Detector CPU · p95'], ['controller_cpu_percent_mean', 'Controller CPU · mean'],
  ['controller_cpu_percent_p95', 'Controller CPU · p95'], ['telemetry_bandwidth_kbps', 'Telemetry bandwidth'],
  ['openflow_bandwidth_kbps', 'OpenFlow bandwidth'], ['flow_table_entries', 'Flow-table entries'],
];

export default function App() {
  const [runs, setRuns] = useState<RunSummary[]>([]);
  const [overview, setOverview] = useState<Overview | null>(null);
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState('');
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<RunSummary | null>(null);
  const [series, setSeries] = useState<Series>(emptySeries);
  const [listLoading, setListLoading] = useState(true);
  const [detailLoading, setDetailLoading] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState('');
  const [detailError, setDetailError] = useState('');
  const [updatedAt, setUpdatedAt] = useState<Date | null>(null);
  const [autoRefresh, setAutoRefresh] = useState(true);
  const [refreshKey, setRefreshKey] = useState(0);
  const refresh = useCallback(() => setRefreshKey(key => key + 1), []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const controller = new AbortController(); let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
    const load = async () => {
      try {
        const [nextRuns, nextOverview] = await Promise.all([getRuns(controller.signal), getOverview(controller.signal)]);
        if (controller.signal.aborted) return;
        setRuns(nextRuns); setOverview(nextOverview); setError(''); setUpdatedAt(new Date());
        setSelectedId(current => nextRuns.some(run => run.run_id === current) ? current : nextRuns[0]?.run_id || '');
      } catch (e) { if (!controller.signal.aborted) setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Could not connect to the experiment server.'); }
      finally {
        if (!controller.signal.aborted) { setListLoading(false); if (autoRefresh) timer = setTimeout(load, POLL_MS); }
      }
    };
    void load();
    return () => { controller.abort(); clearTimeout(timer); };
  }, [autoRefresh, refreshKey]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!selectedId) { setSelected(null); setSeries(emptySeries); return; }
    const controller = new AbortController(); let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
    setSelected(null); setSeries(emptySeries); setDetailError(''); setDetailLoading(true);
    const load = async () => {
      try {
        const [run, data] = await Promise.all([getRun(selectedId, controller.signal), getSeries(selectedId, controller.signal)]);
        if (!controller.signal.aborted) { setSelected(run); setSeries(data); setDetailError(''); }
      } catch (e) { if (!controller.signal.aborted) setDetailError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Could not load this run.'); }
      finally {
        if (!controller.signal.aborted) { setDetailLoading(false); if (autoRefresh) timer = setTimeout(load, POLL_MS); }
      }
    };
    void load();
    return () => { controller.abort(); clearTimeout(timer); };
  }, [selectedId, autoRefresh, refreshKey]);

  const comparisons = useMemo(() => selected ? compatibleRuns(runs, selected).sort((a, b) => a.sampling_rate - b.sampling_rate || a.seed - b.seed) : [], [runs, selected]);
  return <>
    <a className="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to experiment results</a>
    <header className="topbar"><div className="brand"><span className="brand-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i /><i /><i /></span><span>M3<span className="brand-divider"> / </span><span className="brand-light">Observatory</span></span></div><span className="topbar-subtitle">ADAPTIVE DDOS DETECTION</span><span className="project-tag">5G-NIDD · SDN</span></header>
    <main id="main">
      <div className="page-heading"><div><div className="eyebrow">EXPERIMENT WORKSPACE <span>01 / M3</span></div><h1>Less telemetry. <span>Measured detection.</span></h1><p>Sampling, adaptive learning, and the evidence behind every result.</p></div><div className="refresh-tools"><label className="refresh-toggle"><input type="checkbox" checked={autoRefresh} onChange={e => setAutoRefresh(e.target.checked)} />Auto-refresh · 3s</label><button onClick={refresh} className="button"><span aria-hidden="true">↻</span> Refresh</button></div></div>
      <div className="connection-line" role="status"><span className={`connection-dot ${error ? 'offline' : updatedAt ? 'online' : ''}`} />{error ? 'Evidence connection unavailable' : updatedAt ? `Connected · updated ${updatedAt.toLocaleTimeString()}` : 'Connecting to experiment server…'}{!autoRefresh && <span className="paused-label">Polling paused</span>}</div>
      {error && <div className="error-banner" role="alert"><strong>Could not refresh experiments.</strong><span>{error} {runs.length ? 'Previously loaded evidence remains visible.' : 'Start the FastAPI server on port 8000, then refresh.'}</span></div>}
      <section className="overview-strip" aria-label="Experiment overview">{[['Saved runs', overview?.total_runs], ['Completed', overview?.completed_runs], ['Running', overview?.running_runs], ['Failed', overview?.failed_runs]].map(([label, value]) => <div key={String(label)}><span>{label}</span><strong>{value === undefined ? '—' : number(Number(value))}</strong></div>)}<div className="overview-description"><span>METHOD</span><strong>Hoeffding Adaptive Tree <span>+ ADWIN</span></strong></div></section>
      {listLoading ? <div className="state-panel" role="status"><span className="loader" /><h2>Loading experiment evidence</h2><p>Reading saved runs and current experiment status.</p></div> : !runs.length ? <div className="state-panel"><div className="empty-icon" aria-hidden="true">⌁</div><div className="eyebrow">{error ? 'WAITING FOR EXPERIMENT EVIDENCE' : 'READY FOR THE FIRST RUN'}</div><h2>{error ? 'Connect the experiment server' : 'No experiment results yet'}</h2><p>{error ? 'Saved results cannot be checked until the experiment server responds. Start the server on port 8000 and refresh this page.' : 'Run the M3 experiment runner with verified official 5G-NIDD data. Saved results will appear here automatically.'}</p>{!error && <div className="empty-steps"><span>01 · Verify dataset</span><span>02 · Run N = 1 baseline</span><span>03 · Compare sampling rates</span></div>}</div> : <>
        <section className="run-toolbar" aria-label="Run selection"><div className="run-label"><span className="eyebrow">INSPECT EXPERIMENT</span><label htmlFor="run-select">Selected run</label></div><select id="run-select" value={selectedId} onChange={e => setSelectedId(e.target.value)}>{runs.map(run => <option key={run.run_id} value={run.run_id}>{run.run_id} · N={run.sampling_rate} · {run.scenario} · {run.status}</option>)}</select><div className="selection-count">{runs.length} saved {runs.length === 1 ? 'run' : 'runs'}</div></section>
        {detailError && <div className="error-banner" role="alert"><strong>Run evidence could not be loaded.</strong><span>{detailError} {selected ? 'Shown run details are from the last successful refresh.' : ''}</span></div>}
        {detailLoading ? <div className="state-panel small" role="status"><span className="loader" /><p>Loading selected run…</p></div> : selected && <>
          <section className="run-context"><div className="run-context-head"><div><Badge tone={selected.status}>{selected.status}</Badge><Badge tone={selected.source === 'fixture' ? 'fixture' : 'source'}>{sourceName(selected.source)}</Badge><Badge>{modeName(selected.mode)}</Badge><h2>{selected.scenario.replaceAll('_', ' ')}</h2></div><div className="sampling-emblem"><span>SAMPLING RATE</span><strong>1<span> / </span>{selected.sampling_rate}</strong></div></div><div className="context-bottom"><span>Run <code>{selected.run_id}</code></span><span>Seed {selected.seed}</span><span>Evaluation unit: <strong>{selected.unit}</strong></span><span>Started {dateLabel(selected.created_at)}</span></div></section>
          {selected.source !== 'official_5g_nidd' && <div className="notice">This run is labeled <strong>{sourceName(selected.source)}</strong>. Its results do not establish performance on official 5G-NIDD.</div>}
          <details className="provenance-details"><summary>Dataset and feature provenance</summary><pre>{JSON.stringify({ feature_schema: selected.feature_schema ?? 'Not recorded', provenance: selected.provenance ?? 'Not recorded' }, null, 2)}</pre></details>
          {selected.mode === 'csv_replay' && <div className="notice">This run samples flow records. Packet sampling and live SDN overhead require capture replay or live sFlow measurements.</div>}
          {selected.status === 'failed' && <div className="error-banner" role="alert"><strong>This run failed.</strong><span>{selected.error || 'No error detail was saved.'}</span></div>}
          <section className="metric-grid" aria-label="Detection metrics"><MetricCard name="Precision" metricKey="precision" metric={selected.metrics.precision} caption="How often attack predictions are correct" /><MetricCard name="Recall" metricKey="recall" metric={selected.metrics.recall} caption="Share of labeled attacks detected" /><MetricCard name="F1 score" metricKey="f1" metric={selected.metrics.f1} caption="Balance of precision and recall" /><MetricCard name="Inference latency" metricKey="inference_latency_ms" metric={selected.metrics.inference_latency_ms} caption="Average time per prediction" /></section>
          <section className="panel timeline-panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">DETECTION THROUGH TIME</span><h2>Adaptive learning timeline</h2></div><Badge>{number(selected.drift_count)} drift {selected.drift_count === 1 ? 'alarm' : 'alarms'}</Badge></div><Timeline series={series} unit={selected.unit} threshold={typeof selected.config.threshold === 'number' ? selected.config.threshold : .5} /></section>
          <div className="analysis-grid"><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">ACCURACY × OVERHEAD</span><h2>Sampling trade-off</h2></div></div><Tradeoff runs={comparisons} selectedId={selected.run_id} /></section><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">STREAM ACCOUNTING</span><h2>Every observation accounted for</h2></div></div><dl className="count-list">{Object.entries(selected.counts).map(([key, value]) => <div key={key}><dt>{key.replaceAll('_', ' ')}</dt><dd>{number(value)}</dd></div>)}</dl><div className="account-note">Input and sampling counts are recorded independently from evaluated labels. Warm-up, exclusions, and unlabeled records are retained in the evidence.</div></section></div>
          <section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">COMPATIBLE COMPLETED TRIALS</span><h2>Sampling comparison</h2></div><Badge>{comparisons.length} trials</Badge></div><div className="table-scroll"><table><caption className="sr-only">Individual compatible trials; no implicit averaging of repeated trials.</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Run / seed</th><th scope="col">Sampling</th><th scope="col">F1</th><th scope="col">Recall</th><th scope="col">CPU mean</th><th scope="col">Telemetry</th><th scope="col">Drift alarms</th></tr></thead><tbody>{comparisons.map(run => <tr key={run.run_id} className={run.run_id === selected.run_id ? 'selected-row' : ''}><th scope="row"><button className="run-link" onClick={() => setSelectedId(run.run_id)}>{run.run_id}</button><small>Seed {run.seed}</small></th><td><Badge>1 / {run.sampling_rate}</Badge></td>{['f1', 'recall', 'cpu_percent_mean', 'telemetry_bandwidth_kbps'].map(key => <td key={key}>{formatMetric(key, run.metrics[key])}{run.metrics[key]?.status === 'estimated' && <small>estimated</small>}</td>)}<td>{run.drift_count}</td></tr>)}{!comparisons.length && <tr><td colSpan={7}>No compatible completed trials yet.</td></tr>}</tbody></table></div></section>
          <div className="analysis-grid details-grid"><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">METRIC EVIDENCE</span><h2>Measurements & limitations</h2></div></div><div className="evidence-list">{detailMetrics.map(([key, label]) => <div key={key}><div><strong>{label}</strong><small>{metricValue(selected.metrics[key]) === null ? selected.metrics[key]?.reason || 'No measurement saved.' : selected.metrics[key]?.reason || selected.metrics[key]?.status}</small></div><span>{formatMetric(key, selected.metrics[key])}</span></div>)}</div></section><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">ADWIN / HAT</span><h2>Drift event log</h2></div></div>{series.drift.length ? <ol className="drift-log">{series.drift.map((event, i) => <li key={`${event.index}-${i}`}><span className="event-dot" /><div><strong>{event.event.replaceAll('_', ' ')}</strong><p>{event.detector} · observation {event.index}</p><small>{timeLabel(event.time)}</small></div></li>)}</ol> : <div className="chart-empty compact"><h3>No drift events saved</h3><p>Absence of an alarm does not establish absence of a distribution change.</p></div>}<details className="config-details"><summary>Run configuration and provenance</summary><pre>{JSON.stringify(selected.config, null, 2)}</pre></details></section></div>
        </>}
      </>}
      <footer><span>M3 Observatory <span className="footer-dot">·</span> 5G-NIDD sampled telemetry</span><span>Evidence first. Every number traces to a saved run.</span></footer>
    </main>
  </>;
}
