127 setSelected(null); setSeries(emptySeries); setDetailError(''); setDetailLoading(true);Clears prior selection evidence/errors and enables the detail loading state when this effect starts.
128 const load = async () => {Defines the selected-run asynchronous fetch operation.
129 try {Begins request exception handling.
130 const [run, data] = await Promise.all([getRun(selectedId, controller.signal), getSeries(selectedId, controller.signal)]);Loads the selected summary and its bounded time series concurrently with the same abort signal.
131 if (!controller.signal.aborted) { setSelected(run); setSeries(data); setDetailError(''); }Stores both responses and clears the detail error only if this effect is still active.
132 } catch (e) { if (!controller.signal.aborted) setDetailError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Could not load this run.'); }Reports selected-run failures while ignoring canceled effects.
133 finally {Starts the selected-detail finally block.
134 if (!controller.signal.aborted) { setDetailLoading(false); if (autoRefresh) timer = setTimeout(load, POLL_MS); }Ends detail loading and schedules another selected-detail load after the polling delay when enabled.
135 }Closes the finally block.
136 };Closes the detail load function.
137 void load();Starts the first detail load immediately.
138 return () => { controller.abort(); clearTimeout(timer); };Aborts old detail requests and clears their timeout on effect cleanup, including when selection changes.
139 }, [selectedId, autoRefresh, refreshKey]);Reruns the detail effect for a new selected ID, refresh setting, or manual refresh.
140blankBlank line separates logical sections; no runtime effect.
141 const comparisons = useMemo(() => selected ? compatibleRuns(runs, selected).sort((a, b) => a.sampling_rate - b.sampling_rate || a.seed - b.seed) : [], [runs, selected]);Memoizes compatible completed trials; sorts by sampling N then seed. With no selected summary returns an empty list.
142 return <>Begins returning the entire dashboard as a React fragment.
143 <a className="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to experiment results</a>Provides a keyboard skip link that jumps to the main content element.
144 <header className="topbar"><div className="brand"><span className="brand-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i /><i /><i /></span><span>M3<span className="brand-divider"> / </span><span className="brand-light">Observatory</span></span></div><span className="topbar-subtitle">ADAPTIVE DDOS DETECTION</span><span className="project-tag">5G-NIDD · SDN</span></header>Renders the M3 Observatory header, decorative bar logo, adaptive-detection subtitle, and dataset/project label. Branding is static; evidence provenance is shown per run below.
145 <main id="main">Starts the main semantic content region and supplies the skip link's target ID.
146 <div className="page-heading"><div><div className="eyebrow">EXPERIMENT WORKSPACE <span>01 / M3</span></div><h1>Less telemetry. <span>Measured detection.</span></h1><p>Sampling, adaptive learning, and the evidence behind every result.</p></div><div className="refresh-tools"><label className="refresh-toggle"><input type="checkbox" checked={autoRefresh} onChange={e => setAutoRefresh(e.target.checked)} />Auto-refresh · 3s</label><button onClick={refresh} className="button"><span aria-hidden="true">↻</span> Refresh</button></div></div>Renders the page title and controlled auto-refresh checkbox; the Refresh button calls refresh, restarting both polling effects.
147 <div className="connection-line" role="status"><span className={`connection-dot ${error ? 'offline' : updatedAt ? 'online' : ''}`} />{error ? 'Evidence connection unavailable' : updatedAt ? `Connected · updated ${updatedAt.toLocaleTimeString()}` : 'Connecting to experiment server…'}{!autoRefresh && <span className="paused-label">Polling paused</span>}</div>Announces connection status: current request error, latest successful time, or initial connecting state. Shows Polling paused when automatic requests are disabled.
148 {error && <div className="error-banner" role="alert"><strong>Could not refresh experiments.</strong><span>{error} {runs.length ? 'Previously loaded evidence remains visible.' : 'Start the FastAPI server on port 8000, then refresh.'}</span></div>}Displays an alert for list refresh errors; if prior runs exist says saved evidence remains visible, otherwise offers server-start guidance.
149 <section className="overview-strip" aria-label="Experiment overview">{[['Saved runs', overview?.total_runs], ['Completed', overview?.completed_runs], ['Running', overview?.running_runs], ['Failed', overview?.failed_runs]].map(([label, value]) => <div key={String(label)}><span>{label}</span><strong>{value === undefined ? '—' : number(Number(value))}</strong></div>)}<div className="overview-description"><span>METHOD</span><strong>Hoeffding Adaptive Tree <span>+ ADWIN</span></strong></div></section>Maps four overview counters into cards, shows an em dash until each value exists, and states the method; optional chaining prevents accessing a null overview.
150 {listLoading ? <div className="state-panel" role="status"><span className="loader" /><h2>Loading experiment evidence</h2><p>Reading saved runs and current experiment status.</p></div> : !runs.length ? <div className="state-panel"><div className="empty-icon" aria-hidden="true">⌁</div><div className="eyebrow">{error ? 'WAITING FOR EXPERIMENT EVIDENCE' : 'READY FOR THE FIRST RUN'}</div><h2>{error ? 'Connect the experiment server' : 'No experiment results yet'}</h2><p>{error ? 'Saved results cannot be checked until the experiment server responds. Start the server on port 8000 and refresh this page.' : 'Run the M3 experiment runner with verified official 5G-NIDD data. Saved results will appear here automatically.'}</p>{!error && <div className="empty-steps"><span>01 · Verify dataset</span><span>02 · Run N = 1 baseline</span><span>03 · Compare sampling rates</span></div>}</div> : <>Selects initial loading, no-runs explanation, or the run-content fragment. Empty-state text distinguishes connection failure from a successfully retrieved empty list.
151 <section className="run-toolbar" aria-label="Run selection"><div className="run-label"><span className="eyebrow">INSPECT EXPERIMENT</span><label htmlFor="run-select">Selected run</label></div><select id="run-select" value={selectedId} onChange={e => setSelectedId(e.target.value)}>{runs.map(run => <option key={run.run_id} value={run.run_id}>{run.run_id} · N={run.sampling_rate} · {run.scenario} · {run.status}</option>)}</select><div className="selection-count">{runs.length} saved {runs.length === 1 ? 'run' : 'runs'}</div></section>Renders an accessible controlled run selector showing ID, N, scenario and status for each run; changing selection triggers the detail effect.
152 {detailError && <div className="error-banner" role="alert"><strong>Run evidence could not be loaded.</strong><span>{detailError} {selected ? 'Shown run details are from the last successful refresh.' : ''}</span></div>}Shows selected-detail errors and, if old selected evidence remains, explains that it is from the last successful refresh.
153 {detailLoading ? <div className="state-panel small" role="status"><span className="loader" /><p>Loading selected run…</p></div> : selected && <>Shows selected-run loading first; otherwise renders detail content only when a selected summary exists.
154 <section className="run-context"><div className="run-context-head"><div><Badge tone={selected.status}>{selected.status}</Badge><Badge tone={selected.source === 'fixture' ? 'fixture' : 'source'}>{sourceName(selected.source)}</Badge><Badge>{modeName(selected.mode)}</Badge><h2>{selected.scenario.replaceAll('_', ' ')}</h2></div><div className="sampling-emblem"><span>SAMPLING RATE</span><strong>1<span> / </span>{selected.sampling_rate}</strong></div></div><div className="context-bottom"><span>Run <code>{selected.run_id}</code></span><span>Seed {selected.seed}</span><span>Evaluation unit: <strong>{selected.unit}</strong></span><span>Started {dateLabel(selected.created_at)}</span></div></section>Renders status/source/mode badges, readable scenario, 1/N sampling emblem, ID, seed, unit, and formatted start time.
155 {selected.source !== 'official_5g_nidd' && <div className="notice">This run is labeled <strong>{sourceName(selected.source)}</strong>. Its results do not establish performance on official 5G-NIDD.</div>}Shows a provenance notice for every source except official_5g_nidd so fixture/live results are not represented as official dataset performance.
156 <details className="provenance-details"><summary>Dataset and feature provenance</summary><pre>{JSON.stringify({ feature_schema: selected.feature_schema ?? 'Not recorded', provenance: selected.provenance ?? 'Not recorded' }, null, 2)}</pre></details>Creates a native expandable details panel and pretty-prints feature schema and provenance; missing fields explicitly say Not recorded.
157 {selected.mode === 'csv_replay' && <div className="notice">This run samples flow records. Packet sampling and live SDN overhead require capture replay or live sFlow measurements.</div>}For CSV replay explains that flow-record subsampling does not itself measure packet sampling or live-network overhead.
158 {selected.status === 'failed' && <div className="error-banner" role="alert"><strong>This run failed.</strong><span>{selected.error || 'No error detail was saved.'}</span></div>}Displays a failed-run alert with its saved error or an explicit missing-detail fallback.
159 <section className="metric-grid" aria-label="Detection metrics"><MetricCard name="Precision" metricKey="precision" metric={selected.metrics.precision} caption="How often attack predictions are correct" /><MetricCard name="Recall" metricKey="recall" metric={selected.metrics.recall} caption="Share of labeled attacks detected" /><MetricCard name="F1 score" metricKey="f1" metric={selected.metrics.f1} caption="Balance of precision and recall" /><MetricCard name="Inference latency" metricKey="inference_latency_ms" metric={selected.metrics.inference_latency_ms} caption="Average time per prediction" /></section>Renders precision, recall, F1, and inference latency cards using actual saved metrics and short plain-language captions.
160 <section className="panel timeline-panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">DETECTION THROUGH TIME</span><h2>Adaptive learning timeline</h2></div><Badge>{number(selected.drift_count)} drift {selected.drift_count === 1 ? 'alarm' : 'alarms'}</Badge></div><Timeline series={series} unit={selected.unit} threshold={typeof selected.config.threshold === 'number' ? selected.config.threshold : .5} /></section>Renders the timeline heading and drift-count badge; passes the run's numeric threshold, falling back to .5 if absent/non-numeric.
161 <div className="analysis-grid"><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">ACCURACY × OVERHEAD</span><h2>Sampling trade-off</h2></div></div><Tradeoff runs={comparisons} selectedId={selected.run_id} /></section><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">STREAM ACCOUNTING</span><h2>Every observation accounted for</h2></div></div><dl className="count-list">{Object.entries(selected.counts).map(([key, value]) => <div key={key}><dt>{key.replaceAll('_', ' ')}</dt><dd>{number(value)}</dd></div>)}</dl><div className="account-note">Input and sampling counts are recorded independently from evaluated labels. Warm-up, exclusions, and unlabeled records are retained in the evidence.</div></section></div>Creates the trade-off and observation-accounting columns; Object.entries turns count fields into readable labels and formatted numbers, with a note separating sampled input from evaluated labels.
162 <section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">COMPATIBLE COMPLETED TRIALS</span><h2>Sampling comparison</h2></div><Badge>{comparisons.length} trials</Badge></div><div className="table-scroll"><table><caption className="sr-only">Individual compatible trials; no implicit averaging of repeated trials.</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Run / seed</th><th scope="col">Sampling</th><th scope="col">F1</th><th scope="col">Recall</th><th scope="col">CPU mean</th><th scope="col">Telemetry</th><th scope="col">Drift alarms</th></tr></thead><tbody>{comparisons.map(run => <tr key={run.run_id} className={run.run_id === selected.run_id ? 'selected-row' : ''}><th scope="row"><button className="run-link" onClick={() => setSelectedId(run.run_id)}>{run.run_id}</button><small>Seed {run.seed}</small></th><td><Badge>1 / {run.sampling_rate}</Badge></td>{['f1', 'recall', 'cpu_percent_mean', 'telemetry_bandwidth_kbps'].map(key => <td key={key}>{formatMetric(key, run.metrics[key])}{run.metrics[key]?.status === 'estimated' && <small>estimated</small>}</td>)}<td>{run.drift_count}</td></tr>)}{!comparisons.length && <tr><td colSpan={7}>No compatible completed trials yet.</td></tr>}</tbody></table></div></section>Renders individual compatible trials in a scrollable table. Each ID button selects that run; current row is highlighted; N, F1, recall, CPU, telemetry and drift count are displayed, estimated values marked, and an empty row spans seven columns when none qualify.
163 <div className="analysis-grid details-grid"><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">METRIC EVIDENCE</span><h2>Measurements & limitations</h2></div></div><div className="evidence-list">{detailMetrics.map(([key, label]) => <div key={key}><div><strong>{label}</strong><small>{metricValue(selected.metrics[key]) === null ? selected.metrics[key]?.reason || 'No measurement saved.' : selected.metrics[key]?.reason || selected.metrics[key]?.status}</small></div><span>{formatMetric(key, selected.metrics[key])}</span></div>)}</div></section><section className="panel"><div className="panel-heading"><div><span className="eyebrow">ADWIN / HAT</span><h2>Drift event log</h2></div></div>{series.drift.length ? <ol className="drift-log">{series.drift.map((event, i) => <li key={`${event.index}-${i}`}><span className="event-dot" /><div><strong>{event.event.replaceAll('_', ' ')}</strong><p>{event.detector} · observation {event.index}</p><small>{timeLabel(event.time)}</small></div></li>)}</ol> : <div className="chart-empty compact"><h3>No drift events saved</h3><p>Absence of an alarm does not establish absence of a distribution change.</p></div>}<details className="config-details"><summary>Run configuration and provenance</summary><pre>{JSON.stringify(selected.config, null, 2)}</pre></details></section></div>Builds detailed metric evidence with saved reasons/status, plus the drift-event list or no-alarm explanation. Event keys combine index and position; a native details panel pretty-prints the selected config.
164 </>}Closes the selected-summary fragment and its conditional rendering expression.

167 </main>Closes the main content element.

frontend/src/style.css

Appearance, layout, SVG styling, responsive breakpoints, keyboard focus, and reduced-motion behavior. The source is compressed into nine physical lines; the appendix expands individual rules.

frontend/src/test-fixtures.ts

Synthetic run factory for tests. Invented measurements support assertions; they are not project performance claims.

Complete source

// Synthetic evidence for tests only. Never imported by the application.
import type { RunSummary } from './types';

export const fixtureRun = (id = 'test-run', n = 1, f1 = .8, cost = 10): RunSummary => ({
  schema_version: 1, run_id: id, source: 'fixture', mode: 'csv_replay', status: 'completed',
  sampling_rate: n, seed: 42, scenario: 'baseline', unit: 'flow',
  created_at: '2026-10-11T12:00:00Z', ended_at: '2026-10-11T12:01:00Z',
  counts: { input: 100, sampled: 100, evaluated: 90, warmup: 10, excluded: 0, unlabeled: 0 },
  metrics: {
    precision: { value: .9, unit: 'ratio', status: 'measured', reason: null },
    recall: { value: .7, unit: 'ratio', status: 'measured', reason: null },
    f1: { value: f1, unit: 'ratio', status: 'measured', reason: null },
    inference_latency_ms: { value: .12, unit: 'ms', status: 'measured', reason: null },
    telemetry_bandwidth_kbps: { value: cost, unit: 'kbit/s', status: 'measured', reason: null },
    controller_cpu_percent_mean: { value: null, unit: '%', status: 'unavailable', reason: 'No live controller in CSV replay.' },
  },
  drift_count: 0, error: null, config: { threshold: .5, grace_period: 200, max_records: 100, warmup_records: 10 },
  feature_schema: 'flow-v1', provenance: { sha256: 'test-only' },
});

frontend/src/App.test.tsx

Component tests for empty/error/provenance/selection states using mocked API helpers.

Complete source

import { fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import App from './App';
import * as api from './api';
import { fixtureRun } from './test-fixtures';

vi.mock('./api', () => ({ getRuns: vi.fn(), getOverview: vi.fn(), getRun: vi.fn(), getSeries: vi.fn() }));

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.mocked(api.getRuns).mockResolvedValue([]);
  vi.mocked(api.getOverview).mockResolvedValue({ total_runs: 0, completed_runs: 0, running_runs: 0, failed_runs: 0, best_run_id: null });
  vi.mocked(api.getSeries).mockResolvedValue({ predictions: [], resources: [], drift: [] });
});

describe('experiment dashboard', () => {
  it('shows a useful empty state without invented runs', async () => {
    render(<App />);
    expect(await screen.findByText('No experiment results yet')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText('Selected run')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('02 · Run N = 1 baseline')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
  it('shows server failures with a recovery action', async () => {
    vi.mocked(api.getRuns).mockRejectedValue(new Error('HTTP 503'));
    render(<App />);
    expect(await screen.findByRole('alert')).toHaveTextContent('HTTP 503');
    expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /Refresh/ })).toBeEnabled();
  });
  it('identifies fixtures, missing metrics and changes the selected run', async () => {
    const a = fixtureRun('trial-a'); const b = fixtureRun('trial-b', 10);
    vi.mocked(api.getRuns).mockResolvedValue([a, b]);
    vi.mocked(api.getOverview).mockResolvedValue({ total_runs: 2, completed_runs: 2, running_runs: 0, failed_runs: 0, best_run_id: null });
    vi.mocked(api.getRun).mockImplementation(async id => id === 'trial-b' ? b : a);
    render(<App />);
    expect(await screen.findByText('This run samples flow records. Packet sampling and live SDN overhead require capture replay or live sFlow measurements.')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('No live controller in CSV replay.')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText(/Its results do not establish performance/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    fireEvent.change(screen.getByLabelText('Selected run'), { target: { value: 'trial-b' } });
    await waitFor(() => expect(api.getRun).toHaveBeenCalledWith('trial-b', expect.any(AbortSignal)));
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByLabelText('Selected run')).toHaveValue('trial-b'));
  });
});

frontend/src/api.test.ts

HTTP-boundary and schema checks with mocked fetch responses.

Complete source

import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { getRun, getRuns, getSeries, validateRun } from './api';
import { fixtureRun } from './test-fixtures';

afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals());
describe('API contract', () => {
  it('accepts versioned evidence and rejects malformed metric values', () => {
    expect(validateRun(fixtureRun()).run_id).toBe('test-run');
    expect(() => validateRun({ ...fixtureRun(), schema_version: 2 })).toThrow('schema version 1');
    const bad = fixtureRun(); bad.metrics.f1.value = Number.NaN;
    expect(() => validateRun(bad)).toThrow('invalid metric evidence');
  });
  it('surfaces HTTP failures rather than displaying blank evidence', async () => {
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ ok: false, status: 503 }));
    await expect(getRuns()).rejects.toThrow('HTTP 503');
  });
  it('encodes selected run IDs and validates response', async () => {
    const mock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, json: async () => fixtureRun('a/b') });
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', mock);
    await getRun('a/b');
    expect(mock.mock.calls[0][0]).toBe('/api/runs/a%2Fb');
  });
  it('rejects invalid series', async () => {
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, json: async () => ({ predictions: [], drift: [] }) }));
    await expect(getSeries('test')).rejects.toThrow('invalid timeline evidence');
  });
});

frontend/src/evidence.test.ts

Pure-function tests protecting missing-value handling, compatible comparisons, and Pareto classification.

Complete source

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { compatibleRuns, formatMetric, paretoRuns } from './evidence';
import type { RunSummary } from './types';
import { fixtureRun } from './test-fixtures';

describe('scientific evidence handling', () => {
  it('keeps measured zero distinct from unavailable', () => {
    expect(formatMetric('recall', { value: 0, unit: 'ratio', status: 'measured', reason: null })).toBe('0.0%');
    expect(formatMetric('recall', { value: null, unit: 'ratio', status: 'unavailable', reason: 'No attacks' })).toBe('Unavailable');
    expect(formatMetric('recall', { value: 0, unit: 'ratio', status: 'unavailable', reason: 'Missing' })).toBe('Unavailable');
  });
  it('does not combine different source, scenario, mode, feature or dataset evidence', () => {
    const base = fixtureRun();
    const different: RunSummary[] = [
      { ...base, source: 'official_5g_nidd' }, { ...base, scenario: 'unseen' },
      { ...base, mode: 'live_sflow' }, { ...base, feature_schema: 'other' },
      { ...base, provenance: { sha256: 'other' } }, { ...base, status: 'running' },
      { ...base, config: { ...base.config, max_records: 200 } },
      { ...base, config: { ...base.config, threshold: .8 } },
    ];
    expect(compatibleRuns([base, ...different], base)).toEqual([base]);
  });
  it('identifies strict Pareto dominance and excludes estimated costs', () => {
    const a = fixtureRun('a', 1, .8, 10);
    const b = fixtureRun('b', 2, .85, 5);
    const c = fixtureRun('c', 5, .7, 2);
    const estimated = fixtureRun('estimate', 10, .99, .1);
    estimated.metrics.telemetry_bandwidth_kbps.status = 'estimated';
    expect([...paretoRuns([a, b, c, estimated], 'telemetry_bandwidth_kbps')]).toEqual(['b', 'c']);
  });
});

frontend/src/integration.test.tsx

Optional read-only real-server checks. Skipped unless M3_API_URL is configured; the server must already contain expected runs.

Complete source

import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import App from './App';
import { getOverview, getRun, getRuns, getSeries } from './api';
import { compatibleRuns } from './evidence';

// Optional read-only integration check against an actual local API.
// No runs are created and no test data is written to the experiment repository.
const apiBase = (globalThis as unknown as { process: { env: Record<string, string | undefined> } }).process.env.M3_API_URL;
const actualFetch = globalThis.fetch;
afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals());

function connect() {
  // jsdom AbortSignal belongs to a different realm than Node's native fetch.
  vi.stubGlobal('fetch', (path: string, options?: RequestInit) => actualFetch(`${apiBase}${path}`, { ...options, signal: undefined }));
}

describe.skipIf(!apiBase)('real local experiment evidence', () => {
  it('accepts every saved summary and series and isolates comparison groups', async () => {
    connect();
    const runs = await getRuns();
    const overview = await getOverview();
    expect(overview.total_runs).toBe(runs.length);
    expect(runs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const run of runs) {
      expect((await getRun(run.run_id)).run_id).toBe(run.run_id);
      const series = await getSeries(run.run_id);
      expect(Array.isArray(series.predictions)).toBe(true);
      for (const candidate of compatibleRuns(runs, run)) {
        expect(candidate.source).toBe(run.source);
        expect(candidate.mode).toBe(run.mode);
        expect(candidate.feature_schema).toBe(run.feature_schema);
      }
    }
  }, 20000);

  it('renders a real official run with its timeline and provenance', async () => {
    connect();
    const runs = await getRuns();
    const official = runs.find(run => run.source === 'official_5g_nidd' && run.status === 'completed' && run.counts.evaluated > 0);
    expect(official).toBeDefined();
    render(<App />);
    const select = await screen.findByLabelText('Selected run', {}, { timeout: 10000 });
    fireEvent.change(select, { target: { value: official!.run_id } });
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByText('Official 5G-NIDD')).toBeInTheDocument(), { timeout: 10000 });
    expect(await screen.findByRole('img', { name: /Prediction timeline/ })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText('Dataset and feature provenance')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getAllByText(official!.provenance!.sha256!, { exact: false }).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(screen.queryByText('This run is labeled', { exact: false })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  }, 20000);

  it('renders actual live collection with a distinct source and no official-data claim', async () => {
    connect();
    const runs = await getRuns();
    const live = runs.find(run => run.source === 'live_sflow' && run.mode === 'live_sflow');
    expect(live).toBeDefined();
    render(<App />);
    const select = await screen.findByLabelText('Selected run', {}, { timeout: 10000 });
    fireEvent.change(select, { target: { value: live!.run_id } });
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getAllByText('Live telemetry').length).toBeGreaterThan(0), { timeout: 10000 });
    expect(screen.getByText('Live sFlow')).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText(/Its results do not establish performance on official/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByText('Official 5G-NIDD')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  }, 20000);
});

frontend/README.md

Human setup instructions and evidence interpretation summary.

Complete source

# M3 Observatory

React + TypeScript dashboard for the M3 FastAPI experiment server. It reads saved evidence and polls every three seconds. The application contains no demonstration data or fabricated experiment values.

## Run

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:5173 with the FastAPI server on http://127.0.0.1:8000. Vite proxies `/api` to the backend. For a packaged deployment, serve `dist/` from FastAPI or configure the reverse proxy to route `/api` to that server.

```sh
npm test
npm run build
```

Optional read-only integration checks against a running API with official CSV and live collector results:

```powershell
$env:M3_API_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000'
npm test -- --run src/integration.test.tsx
```

These checks read existing experiments and never create runs or write synthetic evidence.

## Evidence interpretation

- Source and execution mode appear on every selected experiment.
- Unavailable measurements display their reason, never a replacement zero.
- Comparison is restricted to completed runs matching source, mode, scenario, observation unit, feature schema, dataset checksum, and model/window/warm-up/record-limit settings.
- Each comparison row is an individual trial. The Pareto plot uses measured F1 and measured overhead only; it does not automatically select a knee point.
- Timelines request up to 1,000 predictions and show the returned series without inventing missing observations.
- Live runs and saved runs share the same read-only result contract. Execution is controlled by the experiment runner.

Synthetic fixtures exist exclusively in tests.

Compressed CSS expanded into rules and declarations

CSS lines 3–9 contain many adjacent rules. A selector space means descendant, > means direct child, .name matches a class, and :hover/:focus-visible select interaction states. Comma-separated selectors share declarations. Later matching rules can override earlier ones. px is a CSS pixel, rem is root-font-relative, vw is viewport-width-relative, % depends on its context, and fr divides grid space. Eight-digit hex colors include opacity in the final two digits.

Every declaration below is reproduced in source order. var(--name) reuses a theme variable. These rules control appearance and do not alter the learning model.

frontend/package-lock.json

npm generates this file to record exact resolved dependency versions, package locations, integrity hashes, and the dependency graph. package.json declares acceptable ranges; package-lock.json pins a particular installation. npm ci uses it for a reproducible clean dependency install and fails if it disagrees with package.json. Commit intentional lockfile changes with dependency changes; let npm generate the entries instead of editing hashes/versions manually. Its repeated generated entries are package metadata, rather than custom DDoS detection code. Every physical line is explained in Reference data and generated files.

Follow a run from click to pixels

1. Changing Selected run calls setSelectedId.

2. React starts the selected-run effect; cleanup aborts the old effect's requests and clears its timeout.

3. The effect clears old detail state, shows loading, and fetches summary and series concurrently.

4. api.ts validates responses and returns typed evidence.

5. App stores selected and series and renders context, cards, timeline, and drift log.

6. compatibleRuns creates the eligible trial group; Tradeoff retains measured F1/cost and paretoRuns finds nondominated points.

7. Changing overhead axis recalculates the browser chart; it does not run training or experiments.

8. Polling repeats reads after completion; manual Refresh restarts both request effects.

Explain these before your demo

Be able to explain why TypeScript types do not validate JSON; why unavailable differs from measured zero; why CSV flow sampling cannot establish packet-level overhead; why effect cleanup avoids stale selection results; why missing scores create chart gaps; and why a Pareto frontier does not automatically establish the knee point.

The test sections describe the actual assertions, not a claim that tests were executed during this documentation task. Real-server integration tests depend on existing server evidence.

CSS appendix: 222 individual rules, 684 declarations. Line walkthrough: 17 files, 636 physical lines.

Tests and configuration: every source line explained

This guide documents the source snapshot read for this walkthrough. Each numbered table row corresponds to one physical source line, including blank lines and closing delimiters. The middle column reproduces the line; indentation is retained in the inline source text but Markdown may visually collapse it. Read the original file alongside this guide when indentation matters.

How to read the tests

An assert expresses an invariant: the test passes only if its expression is true. pytest.raises(...) passes only if the enclosed operation raises the expected exception; match= additionally checks the message. A test_... function is discovered automatically by pytest. @pytest.mark.parametrize repeats the same test with different input values.

tmp_path is a pytest fixture that gives each test an isolated temporary directory. monkeypatch temporarily replaces a function/attribute and restores it after the test. These names are provided by pytest, not passed from production code. fixture=True in the replay engine explicitly marks fabricated test data so it cannot silently enter official experiment aggregation.

SpyModel records call order and always returns fixed predictions; AlwaysAttack always predicts an attack. Neither implements HAT learning, and their hardcoded latency values are artificial. Only test_real_hat_and_adwin in test_core.py directly exercises the real detector's learning and monitor. Protocol fixture builders create byte layouts for software validation; they do not recreate the official 5G-NIDD experiment.

Passing this suite establishes these particular behaviors. It does not prove publication claims, unseen-attack robustness on the real dataset, performance on all sampling rates and seeds, an actual SDN deployment's resource savings, or a valid knee point. Those require the saved experiments described elsewhere in the project.

Configuration facts that affect interpretation

JSON supplies settings to RunConfig; omitted fields inherit the defaults in src/m3/config.py. Relative paths resolve from the process working directory. Neither JSON file is a data preparation script or training program. CSV replay follows CSV row order and uses row indices as its internal time, so physical detection delay is unavailable for that mode. CSV sampling is seeded Bernoulli row selection with probability 1 / sampling_rate, not a claim of packet-level sFlow.

scenario="drift" records the scenario name; it does not generate a traffic distribution change. A drift experiment needs suitably ordered data/traffic and documented boundaries. scenario="unseen" has implemented special treatment: warm-up SYNFlood examples are excluded, and the summary enables the held-out SYNFlood recall. The caller still needs to prepare data and keep tuning separate. A live run learns only where verified labels are actually supplied; ADWIN monitors supervised error and does not invent ground truth.

Run the normal tests through the project's installed environment with pytest; pyproject.toml selects the tests directory and quiet output. The live test uses a short local UDP session, while the lab tests mock OVS subprocess output. This documentation task reads and explains the tests; it does not claim a new test execution.

tests/test_core.py

Configuration validation, feature leakage prevention, metrics, data provenance, sampled windows, protocol decoding, test-then-train order, persisted failure evidence, API behavior, Pareto filtering, aggregation, and an actual HAT/ADWIN smoke test.

Reproducibility notes

The Python dependency declarations are version ranges, not a complete exact-version environment lock. Reproducing a research run also needs the actual installed versions, input hashes, configuration, seed, software revision, and raw saved outputs. Frontend package-lock.json records the npm dependency tree and integrity metadata for reproducible dependency installation; its generated package entries are not manually authored application behavior and are explained by purpose rather than line by line in this guide. Markdown documents explain usage and evidence; they are prose, not executable source.

Reference JSON: provenance and dependency identity

These are structured records rather than model algorithms. Every physical line is paired below so a field can be understood without mistaking metadata for runtime detection logic. Repeated archive/package entries follow the same schema. Hash strings are byte fingerprints; their individual characters are not instructions.
